title: When Should You Sell a Stock? Use a Reason, Not a Price Feeling
summary: A beginner-friendly sell checklist based on goals, thesis changes, concentration, risk, taxes and fees—not fear after a price move.
body_markdown:
## Sources and further reading


Checked July 16, 2026. Community posts and videos are included as perspectives; official sources carry the factual authority.


1. [Evaluating Performance](https://www.finra.org/investors/investing/investing-basics/evaluating-performance)


FINRA · regulator


Plan-based performance review, total-return calculation, benchmarks, fees, and rebalancing context.


2. [Beginners’ Guide to Asset Allocation, Diversification, and Rebalancing](https://www.investor.gov/additional-resources/general-resources/publications-research/info-sheets/beginners-guide-asset)


Investor.gov · government


Diversification, allocation drift, three rebalancing methods, and possible tax or transaction-cost consequences.


3. [Analyzing Analyst Recommendations](https://www.sec.gov/about/reports-publications/investorpubsanalystshtm)


U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission · regulator


Warns against relying solely on an analyst recommendation for a buy, hold, or sell decision and identifies possible conflicts.


4. [Publication 550: Investment Income and Expenses](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p550)


Internal Revenue Service · government


Official current reference for investment income, holding periods, capital gains and losses, basis, dividends, and wash sales.


5. [How Do You Decide When to Revisit or Trim a Position?](https://www.reddit.com/r/ValueInvesting/comments/1tzs4qd/how_do_you_decide_when_to_trim_a_position_or/)


Reddit — r/ValueInvesting · community


Illustrates why investors benefit from recording the original thesis, invalidation conditions, risks, and target exposure. Perspective only.
